title: Push yourself: optional extras
one: Four extras for anyone who wants more. None of them is needed.

screens.title: Meet the four extras before you pick one
screens.done: you have saved your project and picked an extra, or none
screens.goal: Everything my program needs is done. I can pick any extra, or none.

blocks.p: Everything your program needs is done, so this chapter is for fun.
Four extras: three tries at login, faster swaps, the best attempt, a coloured group.
Pick any one, or none. Press the big button, then click the extra's number in the row of parts above.

blocks.watch: Save your project before you start an extra, so you can always go back.

stages.title: Login: three tries, then no more

screens.title: Make the login stop after three wrong tries
screens.goal: After three wrong passwords the Login button goes grey.

open.what: A counter remembers the wrong tries. On the third one a message shows and the Login button goes grey.
open.does: When it works, nobody can keep guessing the password for ever.

screens.title: Add a counter for wrong tries
screens.done: line 1 is typed above public frmLogin and has no red squiggles
screens.goal: One line at the top of the login code makes a counter called tries that starts at 0.

blocks.p: Open frmLogin's code, where two places change.
Click the empty line above public frmLogin and type the line below.

code.title: A counter for wrong tries
code.where: near the top of frmLogin's code, above the line public frmLogin
partLines: A counter that starts at 0
A whole number called tries. It sits outside every button, so it keeps its value between clicks.

blocks.watch: Type this line above public frmLogin, not inside btnLogin_Click. Inside the button, it would start again at 0 on every click.

screens.title: Switch Login off on the third wrong try
screens.done: lines 1 to 6 are typed and the code has no red squiggles
screens.goal: On the third wrong try, a message shows and the Login button goes grey.

blocks.p: Find the Login incorrect message near the bottom of btnLogin_Click.
Two lines below it, tbxPassword is cleared.
Click at the end of that tbxPassword line and press Enter.

code.title: Count the wrong tries
code.where: near the bottom of btnLogin_Click, under the line that clears tbxPassword
partLines: One more wrong try
Add 1 to tries each time the login is wrong.
On the third, stop
When tries is 3, a message shows. Then the Login button goes grey.

screens.title: Try the three tries
screens.done: every row is ticked, or you have gone where its link says
screens.goal: I type a wrong password three times and the Login button goes grey.

blocks.p: Run your program and then try each row.

check.what: Type a wrong password and click Login. Do it three times.
check.how: On the third try, the message shows. The Login button goes grey.
check.fix: Look at the code on screen 2-2.

check.what: After the third wrong try, type the right username and password.
check.how: Login must NOT work, because the button is grey.
check.fix: If it works, look at the code on screen 2-2.

stages.title: Reaction test: the swaps speed up

screens.title: Make the pictures swap faster as the clock runs down
screens.goal: The reaction test gets harder towards the end.

open.what: The reaction test swaps its pictures once a second. This extra makes the swaps speed up as the clock runs down.
open.does: When it works, the test gets harder towards the end.

screens.title: Make the pictures swap faster each second
screens.done: lines 1 to 4 are typed and the code has no red squiggles
screens.goal: Every second the gap between swaps shrinks by a tenth of a second, down to 0.3 seconds.

blocks.p: Open frmTest's code and find tmrCountdown_Tick.
Its first line takes 1 off CountdownValue.
Click at the end of that line and press Enter.

code.title: Faster swaps
code.where: inside tmrCountdown_Tick, under the line that takes 1 off CountdownValue
partLines: Still slower than 0.3 seconds?
Only when the gap between swaps is more than 300.
Take a tenth off
The gap gets 100 smaller. 100 is a tenth of a second.

blocks.yours: MY tmrSwap starts at 1000. If YOURS starts lower, it reaches 300 sooner.

screens.title: Try the faster swaps
screens.done: every row is ticked, or you have gone where its link says
screens.goal: I take the test and the swaps get faster as the clock runs down.

blocks.p: Run your program, log in and take the test, then try each row.

check.what: Watch the pictures as the clock counts down.
check.how: The swaps get faster each second.
check.fix: Look at the code on screen 3-1.

check.how: The pictures must NOT go too fast to click. They stay clear enough to click to the end.
check.fix: If they go too fast, look at the code on screen 3-1.

screens.title: Show the best of the three attempts
screens.goal: The attempts heading shows the biggest attempt as well as the average.

open.what: The average button already works out the average. This extra also finds the biggest of the three attempts and shows it.
open.does: When it works, the attempts heading shows the best attempt too.

screens.title: Show the best of the three attempts
screens.done: lines 1 to 10 are typed and the code has no red squiggles
screens.goal: After the average, the attempts heading also shows the biggest of the three attempts.

blocks.p: Open frmDataEntry's code and find btnCalculateAverage_Click.
Click at the end of the line Global.attempt3 = and press Enter.

code.title: The best attempt
code.where: inside btnCalculateAverage_Click, under the three Global.attempt lines
partLines: Start with attempt 1
A whole number called best. It starts as attempt 1.
Is attempt 2 bigger?
When attempt 2 is bigger than best, best becomes attempt 2.
Is attempt 3 bigger?
When attempt 3 is bigger than best, best becomes attempt 3.
Show it
The attempts heading now shows the best attempt.

blocks.yours: MY heading says Swim lengths. Use the words on YOUR heading.

screens.title: Try the best attempt
screens.done: every row is ticked, or you have gone where its link says
screens.goal: I type three attempts and the heading shows the biggest one.

blocks.p: Run your program, log in and enter the details, then try each row.

check.what: Type 5, 6 and 8 as the attempts. Click the average button.
check.fix: Look at the code on screen 4-1.

check.what: Run again. Type 5, 9 and 2. Click the average button.
check.how: The heading must NOT say best: 2. It says best: 9.
check.fix: If it says 2, look at the code on screen 4-1.

screens.title: Turn the group panel green, yellow or red
screens.goal: The group panel takes a colour that matches the group.

open.what: The group panel already shows the group. This extra turns the panel green, yellow or red to match the group.
open.does: When it works, the group panel changes colour as the group appears.

screens.title: Turn the group panel green, yellow or red
screens.done: lines 1 to 12 are typed and the code has no red squiggles
screens.goal: When the group appears, the group panel turns green, yellow or red.

blocks.p: Open frmDataEntry's code and find btnCalculateSwimmingGroup_Click.
Click at the end of the line Global.assignedGroup = and press Enter.

code.title: Colour the group panel
code.where: inside btnCalculateSwimmingGroup_Click, under the Global.assignedGroup line and above the pnlSwimmingGroup.Enabled line
partLines: The top group is green
When the group is Advanced, the panel turns light green.
The middle group is yellow
else if asks a second question. When the group is Intermediate, the panel turns khaki, a soft yellow.
Every other group is red
else catches every other group. It turns the panel light red.

blocks.p: After Calculate the panel is switched off as before, but it keeps its new colour.

blocks.yours: MY groups are Advanced and Intermediate. Use the group names on YOUR task sheet, spelled the same as in chapter 10.

screens.title: Try the coloured group
screens.done: every row is ticked, or you have gone where its link says
screens.goal: I work out a group and the panel turns its colour.

blocks.p: Run your program and do everything up to the group, then try each row.

check.what: Get all 5 quiz questions right. Click 6 winning pictures. Type 8, 8 and 8 as the attempts. Click Calculate.
check.how: YOUR top group shows. The group panel turns green.
check.fix: Look at the code on screen 5-1.

check.what: Run again. Get 1 quiz question right. Click 1 winning picture. Type 2, 2 and 2 as the attempts. Click Calculate.
check.how: The panel must NOT be green. It turns light red.
check.fix: If it is green, look at the code on screen 5-1.
